Flooding Disrupts Slovak Tourism Industry Operations as River Levels Rise

Tourism operators across Slovakia are facing ongoing disruption as severe flooding continues to impact the industry’s own resorts, tour facilities, and attractions. Persistent heavy rainfall over the past week has caused the Morava and Váh rivers to burst their banks, inundating low-lying tourism destinations in the Bratislava, Trnava, and Žilina regions.

Industry sources report that several open-air heritage parks, adventure sports sites, and eco-lodges have suffered extensive water damage. "We have never seen water levels rise so quickly," said Miroslav Sabol, operations manager at the Slovak Adventure Parks Association. "Our river rafting base near Žilina is inaccessible, and the visitor center is under more than a meter of water."

At the time of writing, the flooding remains ongoing, with emergency teams from tourism firms working to reinforce levees on properties they operate and evacuate staff from riverside lodges and campsites. According to the Slovak Tourism Federation, at least 45 sites run by sector firms have been directly impacted, ranging from urban walking tour offices in historic towns to rural mountain guesthouses. Temporary closures have also affected several industry-operated river cruise piers, with moorings and ticketing offices partially submerged.

Staff safety is a top concern. Jana Tóthová, spokesperson for the Federation of Slovak Tourism Workers, said, "Our immediate priority is to ensure all workers at affected sites are accounted for and relocated to safe areas. Several dozen employees have been temporarily housed in company-run facilities on higher ground." The union has called for clear communication from site managers regarding shift changes and evacuation procedures.

Experts note that the sector faces significant operational and financial strain as the situation develops. "If the rain continues, recovery could be lengthy for smaller operators without extensive resources," commented Gabriel Horváth, a tourism analyst based in Bratislava. "Many of these firms manage their own unique attractions and infrastructure, which are challenging to repair and reopen quickly."

While it is too early to assess the full extent of the damage, the Slovak Tourism Federation has urged member firms to document losses for potential insurance claims and to prepare for a phased reopening once waters recede. The industry’s crisis response committee is set to meet daily until the flooding subsides.
